readiness.guidance: Without objective recovery metrics, training must remain conservative and prioritise aerobic integrity and neuromuscular freshness over volume or intensity.

monthly_review.summary: August shows reduced volume and slower average pace versus July, with a notable drop in cadence and efficiency decline after strong gains in June–July; the shift toward lower-intensity running (43% Z1) may reflect fatigue management or reduced stimulus.
monthly_review.highlight: Cadence rebounded sharply from 118 spm in July to 149 spm in August — a 31 spm increase — suggesting either improved neuromuscular coordination or a strategic shift away from fatigued, heavy-footed efforts seen in July's low-cadence, high-Z4/Z5 distribution.

goal_tracker.message: To match last month’s 82.4 km would require 31.1 km across just 4 remaining sessions — an unsustainable ~7.8 km/session average, especially given missing recovery data and declining efficiency. Chasing this number is inadvisable without evidence of restored readiness.

insights.title: Z1 dominance masks underlying fatigue adaptation
insights.body: Z1 rose from 19% in July to 43% in August while Z4 dropped from 18% to 8% and Z5 vanished — consistent with reduced neuromuscular output (cadence jumped but only after July’s abnormally low 118 spm) and likely compensatory pacing to preserve aerobic decoupling (aerobic TE improved to 2.6%).

insights.title: Efficiency worsened despite better aerobic TE and lower HR
insights.body: Running economy declined from 13.64 to 14.12 ml/kg/km even as average HR fell (141 → 134 bpm) and aerobic TE improved (2.9% → 2.6%), indicating possible gait inefficiency — supported by vertical oscill holding steady (~7.7–7.9 mm) while ground contact time increased in the 8 km run (301 ms) and spiked to 385 ms in the 8.0 km easy run on 8/23.

insights.title: Pace inconsistency reflects unclear effort calibration
insights.body: Best pace improved to 7:33 min/km (453 sec/km) in August, yet the longest run (12.0 km) was at 8:38 min/km — 65 sec/km slower — and included elevated aerobic TE (3.5%), suggesting compromised late-run efficiency; contrast with June’s 6:32 best pace (392 sec/km) achieved during a 11.1 km longest run.

recommendations.action: Zone 2 run, HR 128–135 bpm, 6.0 km on Tuesday — focus on cadence consistency (target 152±2 spm) and ground contact <305 ms per Garmin feedback
recommendations.reason: Cadence rebounded but remains volatile; reinforcing neuromuscular rhythm at low HR supports aerobic integrity without load escalation.

recommendations.action: Complete 20 minutes of post-run mobility: 5 min foam roll quads/hamstrings, 10 min dynamic hip + ankle drills, 5 min diaphragmatic breathing — immediately after every run
recommendations.reason: Vertical oscill unchanged despite efficiency decline suggests stiffness or restricted range; mobility counters rising ground contact time (e.g., 385 ms on 8/23).

recommendations.action: Skip all Zone 4+ efforts for next 7 days; replace planned threshold/hill work with Zone 2 strides: 4 × 20 sec @ Z3 (HR 145–150), walk 60 sec recovery, total time <15 min
recommendations.reason: Z4 dropped sharply (18% → 8%) and Z5 disappeared — reintroducing intensity before confirming recovery markers is premature and risks reinforcing inefficient mechanics.

risk_flags.evidence: Running economy declined (13.64 → 14.12 ml/kg/km) while ground contact time spiked to 385 ms on 8/23 and vertical oscill remained elevated (6.6–8.0 mm)
risk_flags.action: Prioritise mobility and cadence-aware Zone 2 before reintroducing sustained Z3+ efforts

risk_flags.evidence: 12.0 km long run at 8:38 min/km showed 3.5% aerobic decoupling — highest in recent runs — despite avg HR of 146 bpm, suggesting cardiovascular strain outpacing perceived effort
risk_flags.action: Use HR-guided pacing exclusively for long runs until aerobic TE stabilises ≤2.5% across ≥2 consecutive long runs

weekly_focus.description: Re-establish neuromuscular coordination and aerobic pacing consistency through cadence-anchored Zone 2 work, mobility-driven ground contact reduction, and strict HR-governed effort — no reliance on pace alone.
suggested_sessions: Mobility-first easy run with post-run routine
